title: Use calibrated stopping only within intake safety and reviewer capacity
observed_evidence: Oracle household states share household-level dependence. The corrected certification API applies simultaneous binomial bounds over a fixed threshold grid and abstains when infeasible.
executive_recommendation: Test calibrated questioning as an intake aid with mandatory escalation. Do not monetize an unsafe benefits commitment away: its maximum rate is a separate feasibility constraint.
priorities: Hold out entire households and freeze the stopping grid before calibration.
Budget escalation work and question burden together.
Choose a policy only when the safety gate and staffed queue capacity both hold.
reversal: If no threshold is certifiable or escalations exceed capacity, the result is hold/increase staffing, not forced automation.
uncertainty: Oracle states are not observed applicant conversations. Zero monetized harm in this model means harm is governed by a hard gate, not that harm has no value.

economics.evidence_status: ILLUSTRATIVE ASSUMPTIONS, NOT MEASURED COSTS OR RISK

product.randomization_unit: caseworker account; all households handled by an account share assignment
product.retention_interpretation: caseworker uses the workflow for another eligible household
